unit.why: A talmudic legend from the Yerushalmi (Shabbat 6) about two students of R. Hanina saved from a predicted death by an act of charity; it has no Hasidic figures.

stories.start_quote: מעשה בשני תלמידים מתלמידי ר' חנינא
stories.summary_en: An astrologer predicts that two students of R. Hanina going out to cut wood will not return; they share their bread with a starving old man who blesses them, and they come back safely, while a snake cut in two is found in their load, so the astrologer admits that charity overrides his stars.

tags.why: A talmudic tale copied from the Yerushalmi, praising the merit of rabbinic students
An exemplary tale of charity saving from death, in a collection titled Maasim Tovim

quotes: שברו וחתכו את הלחם ונתנו לו את החצי
tags.why: They give half their bread to the hungry old man
They are saved from the snake without noticing it

quotes: מה אעשה לאלהי ישראל הוא מתפייס בחצי ככר לחם
tags.why: The astrologer is presumably a gentile who acknowledges the God of Israel
The old man prays for them

quotes: אני איש כזב ואין ממש באצטגנינות שלי
tags.why: The astrologer admits his art is false

quotes: וישאלו לאלו הב׳ תלמידים מה מצוה באה לידכם
tags.why: The hidden reason for their rescue is uncovered afterwards
